title: Elevated GANAB fuels PD-1/PD-L1 checkpoint-mediated immune escape by maintaining PD-L1 stability in bladder cancer.
authors: Jin, Xuanxuan; Xu, Yi; Ling, Keyu; Li, Haoyu; Wang, Jianzhe; Liu, Jieyu; Yang, Xiangchou; Mu, Haiqi
one_liner_zh: 该文研究膀胱癌中GANAB通过调控PD-L1 N-糖基化介导免疫逃逸，属于肿瘤免疫与蛋白翻译后修饰研究，无蛋白质-DNA互作、结合位点预测或AI/物理模拟建模内容，与本课题无关。
abstract: BACKGROUND: Bladder cancer (BCa) is one of the most common malignancies of the urinary system, with limited treatment options and extremely poor prognosis in advanced stages. Although immune checkpoint inhibitors targeting the PD-1/PD-L1 axis have been approved for clinical use, the objective response rate remains low (15%-25%), and acquired resistance frequently develops. The molecular mechanisms underlying PD-L1-mediated immune evasion in bladder cancer remain incompletely understood. Post-translational modification of PD-L1, particularly N-glycosylation, stabilizes the protein and enhances its immunosuppressive function; however, the specific enzymes regulating this process have not been systematically identified in BCa. METHODS: We analyzed single-cell sequencing data from public databases to identify malignant epithelial subpopulations and constructed prognostic models using high-dimensional weighted gene co-expression network analysis (hdWGCNA), LASSO regression, and machine learning. Crucially, we performed extensive experimental validation beyond bioinformatics prediction: Ganab was stably knocked down in MB49 bladder cancer cells using lentivirus-mediated shRNA, and the effects on cell proliferation and migration were assessed by CCK-8 and wound healing assays. An orthotopic bladder cancer model was established in C57BL/6 mice by intravesical inoculation of MB49-luciferase cells, with tumor growth monitored by live bioluminescence imaging. Tumor tissues were subjected to single-cell RNA sequencing to dissect the tumor immune microenvironment (TIME) at single-cell resolution. Mechanistically, Western blotting, PNGase F deglycosylation, immunofluorescence, and bidirectional co-immunoprecipitation were employed to elucidate how GANAB regulates PD-L1 glycosylation. Flow cytometry and CellChat analysis were used to evaluate T-cell subset remodeling and PD-L1/PD-1 signaling attenuation. RESULTS: We identified a malignant epithelial subpopulation (Epi_3) characterized by high tumor stemness scores and extensive copy number variations. A 15-gene prognostic signature was successfully constructed, in which GANAB exhibited the highest predictive weight. GANAB protein expression progressively increased along the pseudotime trajectory of tumor progression. Experimentally, inhibition of Ganab significantly suppressed MB49 cell proliferation and migration in vitro, and markedly inhibited orthotopic tumor growth in vivo. Mechanistically, GANAB regulated PD-L1 N-glycosylation, yielding two distinct PD-L1 bands: a 45 kDa glycosylated form (Gly-PD-L1) and a 33 kDa non-glycosylated form (Non-gly-PD-L1). Co-immunoprecipitation confirmed that GANAB specifically interacted with non-glycosylated PD-L1 (33 kDa) but not with glycosylated PD-L1 (45 kDa), indicating that GANAB interacts with non-glycosylated PD-L1 and may facilitate its entry into the ER glycosylation pathway. Single-cell analysis of shGanab tumor tissues revealed profound remodeling of the TIME: exhausted T cells (Tex) were reduced, effector memory T cells (Tem) were increased, and PD-L1/PD-1 signaling between tumor cells and T-cell subsets was attenuated. SCENIC analysis identified Stat1 as a key upstream transcription factor, and IMvigor210 cohort analysis confirmed positive correlations among GANAB, STAT1, PD-L1, and CD8A expression. Patients with high GANAB expression exhibited poorer immunotherapeutic responses and worse prognosis. CONCLUSIONS: Our findings establish a robust prognostic model for BCa patients through integrated single-cell and bulk transcriptome analysis. More importantly, we demonstrate through both in vitro and in vivo experiments that the core gene GANAB promotes bladder cancer progression and immune evasion by regulating PD-L1 N-glycosylation along the PD-1/PD-L1 axis, thereby remodeling the tumor immune microenvironment. In the TCGA cohort, GANAB expression correlated strongly with the T-cell-inflamed gene expression profile (TEP; Spearman R = 0.85, P < 2.2e-16), indicating that GANAB-high tumors represent an inflamed yet immunotherapy-resistant phenotype. We acknowledge that the relationship between GANAB and other established biomarkers, including tumor mutation burden and PD-L1 combined positive score, as well as its expression profile across normal tissues, remains to be characterized. Furthermore, specific GANAB inhibitors are currently unavailable, and the ubiquitous expression of GANAB as a housekeeping endoplasmic reticulum enzyme raises potential on-target safety concerns that preclude immediate therapeutic targeting. Therefore, rather than advocating direct GANAB inhibition, we propose that GANAB serves as a candidate stratification biomarker and mechanistic node for glycosylation-mediated checkpoint resistance. Its clinical utility should be evaluated alongside emerging modalities such as ferroptosis-targeted nanomedicines and antibody-drug conjugates, with future efforts focused on biomarker validation and the development of tumor-specific delivery strategies before any therapeutic application can be considered.
abstract_zh: 背景：膀胱癌（BCa）是泌尿系统最常见的恶性肿瘤之一，晚期治疗选择有限且预后极差。尽管靶向PD-1/PD-L1轴的免疫检查点抑制剂已获批用于临床，但客观缓解率仍较低（15%-25%），且获得性耐药频繁发生。PD-L1介导的膀胱癌免疫逃逸的分子机制尚未完全阐明。PD-L1的翻译后修饰，特别是N-糖基化，可稳定蛋白并增强其免疫抑制功能；然而，在膀胱癌中调控该过程的具体酶尚未被系统鉴定。方法：我们分析了公共数据库中的单细胞测序数据，以鉴定恶性上皮细胞亚群，并利用高维加权基因共表达网络分析（hdWGCNA）、LASSO回归和机器学习构建预后模型。关键的是，我们在生物信息学预测之外进行了广泛的实验验证：使用慢病毒介导的shRNA在MB49膀胱癌细胞中稳定敲低Ganab，并通过CCK-8和伤口愈合实验评估其对细胞增殖和迁移的影响。通过膀胱内接种MB49-荧光素酶细胞在C57BL/6小鼠中建立原位膀胱癌模型，并通过活体生物发光成像监测肿瘤生长。对肿瘤组织进行单细胞RNA测序，以单细胞分辨率解析肿瘤免疫微环境（TIME）。在机制层面，采用Western blotting、PNGase F去糖基化、免疫荧光和双向免疫共沉淀来阐明GANAB如何调控PD-L1糖基化。使用流式细胞术和CellChat分析评估T细胞亚群重塑及PD-L1/PD-1信号减弱。结果：我们鉴定了一个以高肿瘤干性评分和广泛拷贝数变异为特征的恶性上皮细胞亚群（Epi_3）。成功构建了15基因预后特征，其中GANAB具有最高的预测权重。GANAB蛋白表达沿肿瘤进展的伪时间轨迹逐渐增加。实验方面，抑制Ganab显著抑制了MB49细胞体外增殖和迁移，并显著抑制了体内原位肿瘤生长。机制上，GANAB调控PD-L1 N-糖基化，产生两种不同的PD-L1条带：45 kDa糖基化形式（Gly-PD-L1）和33 kDa非糖基化形式（Non-gly-PD-L1）。免疫共沉淀证实GANAB特异性与非糖基化PD-L1（33 kDa）相互作用，而非糖基化PD-L1（45 kDa），表明GANAB与非糖基化PD-L1相互作用，可能促进其进入内质网糖基化途径。对shGanab肿瘤组织的单细胞分析揭示了TIME的深刻重塑：耗竭T细胞（Tex）减少，效应记忆T细胞（Tem）增加，肿瘤细胞与T细胞亚群之间的PD-L1/PD-1信号减弱。SCENIC分析鉴定Stat1为关键上游转录因子，IMvigor210队列分析证实GANAB、STAT1、PD-L1和CD8A表达之间存在正相关。GANAB高表达患者表现出较差的免疫治疗反应和更差的预后。结论：我们的发现通过整合单细胞和批量转录组分析，为膀胱癌患者建立了稳健的预后模型。更重要的是，我们通过体外和体内实验证明，核心基因GANAB通过沿PD-1/PD-L1轴调控PD-L1 N-糖基化，促进膀胱癌进展和免疫逃逸，从而重塑肿瘤免疫微环境。在TCGA队列中，GANAB表达与T细胞炎症基因表达谱（TEP；Spearman R = 0.85，P < 2.2e-16）强相关，表明GANAB高表达肿瘤代表一种炎症型但对免疫治疗耐药的表型。我们承认，GANAB与其他已确立的生物标志物（包括肿瘤突变负荷和PD-L1联合阳性评分）之间的关系，以及其跨正常组织的表达谱，仍有待表征。此外，目前尚无特异性GANAB抑制剂，且GANAB作为内质网管家酶的普遍表达引发了潜在的靶向安全性问题，阻碍了直接的治疗靶向。因此，我们不主张直接抑制GANAB，而是提出GANAB作为候选分层生物标志物和糖基化介导检查点耐药的机制节点。其临床效用应与新兴治疗模式（如铁死亡靶向纳米药物和抗体药物偶联物）一同评估，未来的工作应聚焦于生物标志物验证和肿瘤特异性递送策略的开发，之后方可考虑任何治疗应用。
